description: The XMM-Newton Optical Monitor is a 30 cm telescope that images the central part of the X-ray field through six broad-band filters: UVW2, UVM2, UVW1, U, B, and V. ESA distributes effective-area response files for those filters, computed from laboratory component measurements and adjusted using observations of standard stars.
short_description: XMM-Newton Optical Monitor filters UVW2-V, effective areas
facility_description: XMM-Newton is an ESA science mission whose X-ray telescopes are accompanied by the Optical Monitor so the same field can be observed in X-rays and in the ultraviolet and optical.
notes: The Optical Monitor page says the detectors are micro-channel plate intensified CCDs and that photon events are centroided to 1/8 physical pixel, so the OM is a photon-counting detector. The filter-wheel page names the six broad-band filters UVW1, UVM2, UVW2, U, B, and V between 180 nm and 580 nm; a white filter, a magnifier, and two grisms are also in the wheel but are not NJM bands. The bandpass figure page shows throughput curves but does not give numeric edges in text. Wavelength bands and preliminary zeropoints below are from Table 2 of the Mason et al. HTML, which says those zeropoints would be updated after a ground-based programme. U, B, and V zeropoints were set so Vega matches literature values; UV filters were set to Vega magnitude 0.025. The paper says the zeropoint is the magnitude that yields 1 count per second, and the detector centroids incoming photon events, so the OM counts photons rather than integrating energy. Mason et al. is cited on the ESA OM page as K.O. Mason et al. 2001, A&A 365, L36. The arXiv record opened this session gives the journal reference Astron.Astrophys.365:L36-L44,2001 and related DOI 10.1051/0004-6361:20000044. ADS and SciX did not return the abstract, so the bibcode string 2001A&A...365L..36M is not included because that exact key was not read on an opened page. The ESDC terms cover data in the ESA Space Science Archives, list XMM-Newton with the credit line 'Credit: ESA, Name of Proposal PI', and require authorisation before commercial use. The OM response-file page itself states no separate licence. Those files are therefore treated under the archive CC BY-NC terms, which do not clearly allow commercial redistribution. The publication acknowledgement has no final period inside the quotation on the guidelines page.
